title: Nodal SDK fastpath playnote
body:
Purpose
---
This is an informal playnote to capture a very small, repeatable SDK onboarding flow ("fastpath") for engineers who want to go from zero to a functioning local integration in ~10 minutes. Focus: minimal friction, robust telemetry contract, and a tiny CI check that proves end-to-end sample runs.

Intended audience
- Product engineers evaluating Redwood in a prototype
- Internal SDK ambassadors running customer PoCs
- Solutions engineers who need a reliable demo flow

Goals (MVP)
- Provide a 10-minute path that reliably yields -> sample app calling the Redwood hosted API, streaming response, and token-level cost telemetry visible locally.
- Keep examples polyglot (node + python) but intentionally minimal: one canonical JS example + one Python snippet.
- Deliver a one-file runnable sample (no docker, no infra) that exercises: auth, streaming, simple error handling, and a telemetry ping.

Constraints and design tradeoffs- No heavy CLI install: prefer npm/pip single-file runner.
- No advanced SDK features (no adapters/sidecars) in MVP.
- Make telemetry explicit and easy to inspect (stdout + JSON file).
- Prioritize deterministic outputs for smoke-checks in CI (seeded prompts).

10-minute fastpath (runnable outline)
1) Pre-reqs (1 min):
   - Node 18+ installed or Python 3.10+.
   - Redwood API key in REDWOOD_API_KEY env var.
2) Get the single-file runner (30s):
   - JS: curl https://example.com/nodal-fastpath.js -o nodal-fastpath.js  (we will host under CDN)
   - PY: curl https://example.com/nodal-fastpath.py -o nodal-fastpath.py
3) Run (4 min):
   - JS: REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_... node nodal-fastpath.js --prompt "Summarize today's meeting in 2 bullets"
   - PY: REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_... python nodal-fastpath.py --prompt "Summarize today's meeting in 2 bullets"
4) Expected result: streaming tokens print to stdout, final JSON summary printed, telemetry.json created with latency and per-token cost fields.
5) Quick verification (30s):
   - jq .telemetry.total_cost telemetry.json  -> should be > 0 and < 0.10 for short prompts

What the sample file does (JS canonical)- Reads env var, validates key present (fail early).
- Sends single request to Redwood hosted text-generation endpoint with streaming flag.
- Writes token events to stdout as they arrive and appends a concise telemetry object to telemetry.json.
- On non-2xx, prints a short troubleshooting hint (common network or auth) and exits 2.

Telemetry contract (explicit, small)
- telemetry.json (single JSON object) fields: 
  - request_id (string)
  - model (string)
  - prompt_tokens (int)
  - completion_tokens (int)
  - total_cost (float, USD)
  - latency_ms (int)
  - sdk_version (string)
  - host_region (string)
  - debug_notes (list of short strings)

We intentionally keep the contract flat and deterministic. The runner emits one file per run to avoid log collisions in local demos.

CI smoke check (tiny)
Objective: ensure SDK examples remain runnable and deterministic.
- Github action job: checkout -> run node/pip example with seeded prompt -> compare telemetry.total_cost and output digest hash with checked-in golden values.
- If diff: fail and post a short repro command to PR.
- Keep golden values permissive: +/- 5% cost variance, stable digest otherwise.

Failure modes and recovery (notes to self)
- Missing key: print exact env var name + quick link to UX console page.
- 401 vs 403: 401 suggests key malformed; 403 suggests org-level restriction. Provide guidance in error blob.
- Streaming stalls: suggest increasing 'stream_timeout_ms' in example, explain retries vs chunk-duplication.

Edge cases for the fastpath
- Long prompts: runner will auto-bail with an explanatory message and a suggested prompt-shortening helper.
- Network flakiness: runner will attempt 1 retry with backoff for idempotent requests only.
- Local firewall: include a single-line curl check in README snippet.

Docs + UX copy (short)
- Title: "10-minute SDK fastpath: run a streaming sample and see token costs"
- Subhead: "One file, two commands, see what matters: tokens, latency, and cost."
- Steps: condensed into the 10-minute flow above + a one-paragraph explanation of telemetry.json.
- Troubleshooting: quick table (error -> likely cause -> 1-line fix).

Rollout plan (how this document becomes surfaced)
1) Internal pilot: share with 3 solutions engineers and 2 SDK maintainers for dry-run (week 1).
2) Add hosted runner files to static CDN and update sdk repo to include a "get runner" script.
3) Add GitHub action smoke check to the sdk-examples repo (week 2).
4) Ship docs page (short) + console quicklink (week 3).

Open questions / decisions
- Host the single-file runners on CDN vs keep them in repo? CDN makes copying easier but increases sync complexity.
- Should telemetry.json schema be versioned inside the file (telemetry_v = 1)? Pros: explicit upgrades. Cons: extra field for demos. (leaning yes).
- Do we include a minimal test token that can be rate-limited for demos? (security tradeoffs)

TODO (short backlog)
- [ ] Finalize runner code: edge-case tests (Maya)
- [ ] CDN hosting + redirect URL (Infra: Ravi)
- [ ] Add CI smoke action template (Elena)
- [ ] Draft short docs page and UX blurb for console (PM): add link to sample run output
- [ ] Add telemetry_v field and bump contract doc

Quick notes for implementation (developer-facing)
- Keep sample size < 150 lines.
- Prefer fetch/native streaming in node rather than heavy deps.
- Always surface request_id in stdout and telemetry.json.
- Minimal logging: avoid stack traces for common errors; produce friendly localized tips.

Sample snippet (JS, excerpt)
---
const key = process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY;
if (!key) { console.error('Missing REDWOOD_API_KEY — set this and retry.'); process.exit(2); }
// fetch(...streaming flag...)
// write events to stdout as they arrive
// gather per-token counts and write telemetry.json at the end
---

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep copy short; customers hit docs with low attention. One-liner wins.
- Avoid the word "onboarding" in public copy; keep internal use.
- We'll need an internal ticket to keep golden values from drifting when we change default model pricing. Mark that in LINEAR.

Appendix: short checklist for demo-run (for SEs)
- [ ] Confirm REDWOOD_API_KEY scope (hosted demo key).
- [ ] Run curl health check to console endpoint.
- [ ] Run nodal-fastpath.* with seeded prompt.
- [ ] Attach telemetry.json to the support thread if anything odd.

End.
